g.title: Time sequencers and connectors
g.rule:
Use these words to put the events of a story in order and to connect ideas.

reason and resultI ran because I was late. · I was late, so I ran.
contrastAlthough it was dark, we went out. · It was dark, but we went out.
g.ru: Слова для рассказа: first, then, after that, suddenly, in the end. Because — причина, so — результат, although / but — противопоставление.

talk: Tell a short story about a strange or funny evening. Use: first, then, suddenly, in the end.
Why did you start learning English? Use because and so.

r.text:
It was a dark, rainy evening in October. Dana was walking home from work when she saw a small dog under a tree. It was wet and it was shaking.

First she looked for the owner, but the street was empty. Then she gave the dog her sandwich. After that she walked away, but the dog followed her.

She couldn't leave it in the rain, so she took it home. Although her flat was small, she made a bed for it in the kitchen.

The next day she put a photo online. Nobody called. In the end the dog stayed, and now its name is October.

ex.q: When did Dana find the dog?

o: She couldn't leave it in the rain

r.text:
Kurmangazy was one of the most famous Kazakh musicians. He was born about two hundred years ago in a poor family and started to play the dombra when he was a child.

He travelled a lot and wrote more than sixty pieces of music. People loved them, and they still play them today.

Every spring our city has a race for families. It is only three kilometres, but it is not easy.

You start in the main square and run along the river. Then you go over the old bridge and up the hill to the park. In the park you have to climb over a wall and go through a tunnel.

After that you run down the hill, round the lake and across the football pitch. The last part is the hardest: you go up eighty steps to the finish.

Last year my father and I came last. My mother, who was watching, said we walked more than we ran.

I am not a morning person. My alarm goes off at half past six, and I turn it off. Ten minutes later it goes off again.

When I finally get up, I put on my slippers and turn on the coffee machine. I look for my phone. It is usually under the bed.

Then I take off my pyjamas and put on my work clothes. I often put them on too quickly, and at the bus stop I find out that my shirt is inside out.

My wife wakes up at five and goes running. She says I should give up coffee. I am not going to give it up.

script.t: Rustam, your alarm went off at six. Why didn't you turn it off?

talk: Choose three objects near you. Where were they made and what are they used for?
Which invention is the most important for you? Why?

r.text:
We use hundreds of inventions every day, but we don't often think about them.

The ballpoint pen was invented by a Hungarian journalist in the 1930s. He was tired of ink on his fingers. Today millions of pens are sold every day.

The first text message was sent in 1992. It said "Merry Christmas". Now billions of messages are sent every hour.

Tea bags were not planned at all. A tea seller put tea in small bags to send to customers. The customers put the whole bag in hot water, and a new product was born.

Many great ideas are discovered by accident.

ex.q: Who invented the ballpoint pen?

Tea bags were carefully planned.

l.intro: Two students do a quiz about inventions.

script.t: Emma, quiz time. Where was paper invented?
In China. Easy.
Correct. When was the first dishwasher made?
I think it was designed in the nineteenth century.
Yes, in 1886. It was invented by a woman.
Really? And the saxophone?
It was invented by a Belgian. His name was Sax.
Is that true?
Yes. Last one. Where are most phones produced today?
In Asia. Do I win?

talk: What did you use to do at primary school that you don't do now?

r.text:
My grandmother went to school in a village in the 1960s. Her life was very different from mine.

She used to walk four kilometres to school every morning. In winter she used to carry wood for the classroom fire. There didn't use to be a school bus.

The children used to write with pens and ink, and they didn't use to have many books. Her favourite subject was geography, because the teacher used to tell stories about other countries.

Did she use to like school? "I loved it," she says. "It was warm, and my friends were there."

ex.q: How did the grandmother get to school?
What was her favourite subject?

script.t: Mum, did you use to like school?

Yes, we did. A brown dress. It was terrible.

I am a very indecisive person. This morning I couldn't choose between tea and coffee, so I had water.

Now I am planning my holiday. I might go to the mountains, or I might go to the sea. I might travel by train, but it might be too slow.

My friend Aliya is different. She makes up her mind in five seconds. "You might not have a holiday at all if you don't decide," she says.

Take both.

Last year I was travelling to Almaty by train. A man sat down opposite me and started reading a newspaper.
